To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the binding affinities of a set of macrocyclic receptors toward a series of dipeptide ligands have been measured using 1H N MR titrations, and that these affinities show only modest levels of stereoselection.
we synthesized and studied two new macrocylcic compounds that can recognize dipeptides.

We have designed, synthesized, and analyzed a series of macrocyclic receptors that can be regarded as a β-strand of a three-strand β-sheet, with the cross-linking between chains through the 3 and 5 positions of phenylalanine side-chains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of synthetic receptors for the stereospecific recognition of dipeptide ligands.
the design and synthesis of a family of receptors for the stereodifferentiation of dipeptides based on a three-stranded hydrogen-bonded β-sheet motif.
the design and synthesis of a new family of receptors for the stereodifferentiation of peptides, which are based on the hydrogen-bond donor and acceptor pattern of protein β-strands.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the design of macrocyclic receptors based on the hydrogen-bond pattern present in protein β-sheets is feasible and that the receptors show some level of selectivity in their recognition of diamide and dipeptide substrates.
these receptors show moderate levels in the recognition of peptides and diamides and that their selectivities are strongly dependent on the conformation of the ligands.
we have designed a series of receptors that show moderate levels of stereoselection for the recognition of the hydrogen bonding patterns found in the dipeptides and diamides used as ligands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of receptors for the selective binding of peptides is a difficult task.
the hydrogen-bonded recognition pattern in these receptors is not sufficient for the enantioselective and diastereoselecive recognition of diastereomeric dipeptides.
the design of macrocyclic receptors based on a β-sheet hydrogen-bonding motif is not necessarily a good strategy to obtain receptors that are highly enantioselective and diastereoseselective.
